The global scope of this PKGBUILD contains only standard variable assignments, parameter expansions, and a single function definition. No command substitutions (`$(...)`, backticks), arithmetic expansions, `eval`, or external command invocations (`curl`, `wget`) appear in the top-level code. The `package()` function body contains `bsdtar` and `chmod`, but it is **not executed** by `makepkg --printsrcinfo` and is therefore out of scope for this narrow gate. The XML entities (`&apos;`, `&quot;`, `&lt;`, `&gt;`) are an unusual encoding. If treated literally they cause a Bash syntax error on the very first array assignment (`arch=(&apos;x86_64&apos;)`), halting parsing immediately without executing any potentially dangerous commands. If the entities are decoded to their intended characters (`'`, `"`, `<`, `>`), the file is a perfectly ordinary PKGBUILD. In neither scenario does sourcing the file for `--printsrcinfo` run genuinely malicious code.
</details>
